top_findings.title: POST and PUT crash on every request: cowboy_req:read_body/1 result matched as a 2-tuple (breaks R1, R5, R9 over HTTP)
top_findings.evidence: src/books_http_handler.erl:9 and :16 `{Body,R}=cowboy_req:read_body(Req)`; cowboy_req.erl:512 spec returns {ok, binary(), Req}. Live probe: POST /books valid body -> 500, POST without author -> 500 (not 400), PUT /books/1 -> 500; erl log shows badmatch,{ok,<<"{\"title\":\"Dune\"...
top_findings.suggestion: Use `{ok,Body,R}=cowboy_req:read_body(Req)` and add an HTTP-level test

top_findings.title: GET /books crashes on every request, filtered or not: parse_qs/1 test-shim clause returns the raw qs binary (breaks R2, R3)
top_findings.evidence: src/books_http_handler.erl:30 `parse_qs(#{qs:=Qs})->Qs` matches every real Cowboy Req (cowboy_http.erl:829 sets qs => binary); :12 proplists:get_value(<<"author">>, Binary) -> function_clause. Live probe with a row present: GET /books -> 500, GET /books?author=B -> 500
top_findings.suggestion: Drop the map-matching shim clauses and always call cowboy_req:parse_qs/1

top_findings.title: Production handler short-circuits for a fake test Req, so the HTTP 'contract' test exercises nothing
top_findings.evidence: src/books_http_handler.erl:6,32 test_request(#{reply:=_})->true returns Req untouched for /books; :24,26,28,30 map-pattern shim clauses; test/books_api_tests.erl:19-23 http_handler_contract_test passes a hand-built map. The two fatal runtime bugs pass all 4 tests (test_coverage=1.0)
top_findings.suggestion: Remove test-only branches; test against a real started listener (e.g. httpc in eunit/common_test)
